. book launch: dregish history group invite you to a book launch in st eugene's hall, dregish , on fri 13 nov, at 7.30pm; refreshments will be served. the group has produced two books, available at t he event for purchase. one contains a selection of interesting local history articles by members of the dregish history group called'gathering hidden gems on the history of dregish and the people together'. the second is a history of the clergy of adrstraw west by brian devenney, edited by fr mccawille. thank you to nlh fund and rapid for their support. thank you: deborah lowry offers her thanks to all who supported in any way the team hope garden tea party at her home in september. she is most appreciative of the generosity shown by the entire community and is delighted to share that the event raised almost £5,000. the funds raised will support team hope's longer-term development work, helping vulnerable families and communities overseas to build more secure and hopeful futu res. team hope christmas shoe-box appeal for children in africa and eastern europe: you are invited to fill a wrapped shoebox with gifts using the 4ws - something to write, wash, wear and wow, and include a €6 contribution towards transport and delivery. shoeboxes can be dropped off between 1 and 10 nov at castle coffee, or urban barn/pet store, both in castlederg. for further details, labels and guidance, visit

. thank you, from deborah lowry and all at team hope! as our parishes prepare to welcome fr chris next weekend, fr thomas and i take this opportunity to wish him every blessing in his ministry in aghyaran, ardstraw west & castlederg and drumqu in. born in 1986, fr chris is a native of leckpatrick parish. his parents, rosemary and sean , live in strabane. fr chris tells us that his three brothers, two nieces and a nephew form his closest family. following school, chris was employed for several years in an administrative role at the oncology department of altnagelvin hospital. he subsequently pursued seminary studies at st malachy’s college, belfast, and st patrick’s college, maynooth. since ordination in june 2016, fr chris has ministered among the faith communities of st eugene’s cathedral in derry, drumragh (omagh), limavady, kilrea & desertoghill, errigal (garvagh) and granaghan (swatragh). fr chris says that, a fter spending the last five years ‘on the missions’ in co derry, he now looks forward to serving the people of the west tyrone pastoral area. he and kobe (thepet dog) will take up residence in castlederg parochial house at the end of the month. fr chris brings many gifts to his ministry and, in giving generously of himself to serving the people entrusted to his care, i know that he will enjoy the support and encouragem ent of you all. i pray god’s blessing on all that you will share and accomplish together. please keep fr chris in your prayers as he prepares to move to castlede rg and begin the next chapter of his priestly ministry in the west tyrone pastoral area. may god bless you all, fr paul.

a common assumption is that love must just come, that it grows organically, and that it cannot be forced. that’s infatuation, not true love. any kind of love – for a parent, spouse, child, or friend – will reach a point during which it is no longer easy. for love to be true, it must be a free choice and commitment. ‘all your heart, soul, and mind’ sounds rather extreme, even rather dangerous. the world says that loving anyone totally is a risky proposition – what i f the one we love rejects us or lets us down, leaving us with nothing? and the world is even more terrified to love god totally, who cannot even be seen. this makes sense; after all, to love totally is to trust that we will find fulfillment precisely by not looking for it ourselves, but by looking to fulfill someone else. that old, almost clichéd phrase, ‘love grows when i t is given away,’ is actually spot-on in this regard. true love takes a leap of faith, which is what frightens nonbelievers. many people are okay with going to church every now and then or volunteering a charity from time to time (and posting it on instagram, of course). loving like that does not require us to make any kind of leap, any kind of definitive change, any commitment. but loving god with everything means that all we do is for love of him. we trust that he will take care of us. that is heroic; that is what it means to be a saint thought for the day ‘remember that nothing is small in the eyes of god. do all that you do with love.’ saint thérèse of lisieux ‘we have been called to heal wounds, to unite what fallen apart, and to bring home those who have lost their way.’ saint francis of assisi ‘i invite all christians, everywhere, at this very moment, to a renewed personal encounter with jesus christ, or at least an openness to letting him encounte r them; i ask all of you to do this unfailingly each da pope francis (eg 3) chiropodist clinic patricia barne will a end st columbcille centre, clonmany on wed oct 28 from 9am- 2pm. for an appointment call
